newsitem.title: CANADA: QLT rises as Photofrin approved in Germany.
newsitem.headline: QLT rises as Photofrin approved in Germany.

text.p: QLT PhotoTherapeutics Inc stock rose Thursday after the biotechnology company announced it received approval to market its light-activated drug Photofrin in Germany for treatment of early-stage lung cancer.
QLT shares were up 1.30 to 29.85 in Toronto Stock Exchange trading.
German approval means QLT is entitled to receive a US$1 million milestone payment from European marketing partner Beaufour Ipsen.

The approval covers use of Photofrin for the curative treatment of patients with early-stage endobronchial non-small cell lung cancer who are not indicated for surgery or radiotherapy. The company estimated that about 28,000 of these cases are diagnosed in Germany every year.
Stephane Francois, a Beaufour Ipsen executive, said the partners plan to apply for marketing approval of Photofrin in 11 more European countries later this year.
The drug has already been approved for use in treating lung and esophogeal cancer in France and the Netherlands and an application is pending in Italy.

Photofrin is injected in cancer patients and then accumulates in tumor cells. When activated by laser light, the drug produces a toxic form of oxygen that destroys the cancer cells. QLT said the drugs carries low risk of damage to nearby healthy tissue.
